tools.name: request_access
tools.description: Ask the person, or her representative, for access to her record. The request waits for a decision on the service's consent screen; no agent can approve it. Returns the request id and its state.

item_kinds.description:
What each item kind holds:
- mobility: How the person moves and gets places: walking, transfers, stairs, the aids used, driving and rides. A fall goes to falls.
- eating: What and how much the person eats and drinks: appetite, swallowing, diet. Weight goes to vitals.
- medications: What the person takes now, and fills.
- contacts: People and services, and how to reach them: family, friends, neighbors, and others. Clinicians, paid caregivers, and care agencies and facilities go to providers.
- sleep: How the person sleeps and rests.
- appointments: Visits with clinicians, past and upcoming, emergency visits and hospital stays included, and what happened at them as anyone reports it.
- routine: The usual shape of the person's day, regular help included.
- discharge_summary: The summary written when the person leaves a hospital or facility.
- note: Anything no other kind fits, in someone's own words.
- activities: What the person did beyond the usual day: outings, hobbies, exercise, time with people.
- allergies: Allergies and intolerances, and the reaction.
- conditions: Diagnoses: the problem list, or a diagnosis anyone reports.
- test_results: Results of lab tests, imaging, and other tests such as an ECG.
- vitals: Blood pressure, pulse, temperature, oxygen, weight, and blood sugar, measured anywhere, at home included.
- immunizations: Vaccines the person has had.
- procedures: Procedures and surgeries.
- clinical_notes: Clinicians' own notes and letters, other than discharge summaries.
- insurance: Health coverage: plan and payer only, never a member or Medicare number.
- personal_care: Bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, and continence: how the person manages, and the help given.
- memory_and_mood: How the person seems: memory, confusion, mood, and behavior. Observations, not diagnoses.
- symptoms: Changes in how the person feels or looks: pain, cough, swelling, skin, breathing. Observations, not diagnoses.
- falls: Falls and near-falls, and any injury from one.
- living_situation: Where the person lives or is staying now, and with whom.
- care_wishes: Care the person wants or refuses, who may decide about that care, and the papers that say so: an advance directive, a health care proxy, a POLST or DNR.
- equipment: Aids and equipment: hearing aids, glasses, dentures, mobility aids, home medical equipment, implanted devices.
- home: The person's home, in whatever sense the family uses the word: for example the place and keeping it running, repairs, utilities, safety features, access, and who has keys.
- finances: Money for the person and their care: bills, costs, benefits, accounts, and who manages the money.
- providers: Who provides the person's care, in what role, and how to reach them: doctors, nurses, therapists, paid caregivers, home care agencies, hospitals and other facilities, and pharmacies.

tools.name: request_brief
tools.description: Read a brief of the granted item kinds for one purpose. Each claim cites every standing account, with service-asserted fields and the author's text labelled untrusted. Item kinds outside your grant are listed as not available to you. Pass a previous brief's cursor as since_cursor to get only what arrived since.

tools.name: record_observation
tools.description: Append an entry about one item kind under a purpose your grant allows for writing. The author is you, as authenticated from your token, and the user you act for. To correct an entry, write a new one; to withdraw one of your own, set withdraws to its id and leave value empty. If you relay several people, set informant_key to a stable id for each, so their accounts stand separately. media_ids cite media you uploaded for this item kind, and need the person's imagery setting on. scheduled_for is for appointments only. A family member may set topic to a field of the family's they can see, to keep the entry there rather than in its item kind's default topic; a withdrawal goes where its entry is.

tools.name: check_claims
tools.description: Check claims you hold, including ones another agent passed to you, against the record as it stands now. Each claim comes back matches_record, differs_from_record (with problem codes, never values), or not_available if its item kind is outside your grant for this purpose. A match proves the claim matches the record, not that it is true.

tools.name: my_grants
tools.description: List your own active grants and your own pending requests, optionally for one person. Never shows other agents' grants.

tools.name: list_topics
tools.description: For a family member: list the topics of the person's record you can see. Each item kind has a default topic, whose id is the kind, which you see while your grants let you read that kind; fields the family made (ids field-<n>) you see while their audience includes you. Each topic comes with the family's icon and colour. A field's name is a family member's own words, labelled untrusted. A removed field is listed as unfiled.

tools.name: request_topic_brief
tools.description: For a family member: read one topic you can see. For each item kind it can hold, the claim cites every author's standing account in that topic, checked against the record. Pass `on` to see the topic as it was filed at that time, limited to what you can read now. A topic you cannot see is not available to you, the same answer as one that does not exist.

tools.name: propose_field
tools.description: Propose a new field: a name in the family's own words, an optional icon and colour, and entries you can read to put in it. Nothing changes yet: the result is a draft, which you confirm with confirm_proposal, and a new field always goes to the person's decider, who picks who sees it.

tools.name: propose_move
tools.description: Propose moving entries you can read into a topic you can see: a live field, or the default topic of their item kind. The draft says whether it applies on your own confirmation (nobody would start or stop seeing any entry) or goes to the decider.

tools.name: propose_rename
tools.description: Propose a new name for a live field you can see. A rename always goes to the decider.

tools.name: propose_removal
tools.description: Propose removing a live field you can see. Its entries stay in it, shown as unfiled, with the same audience, and can still be moved out. A removal always goes to the decider.

tools.name: propose_style
tools.description: Propose the icon and colour for a topic you can see, a default topic included; null clears either. A style applies on your own confirmation.

tools.name: confirm_proposal
tools.description: Confirm your own draft proposal, saying what your card showed: applies_now or goes_to_decider. If the record would now do something else, the answer is proposal_changed and nothing happens. This is for the family member's own confirmation, not for an assistant to call on its own.

tools.name: my_proposals
tools.description: List your own proposals for a person and the state of each: draft, waiting, applied, denied, or expired. A draft says whether it would apply now or go to the decider.
